text:
alex: Heads up — canary after today's merge shows a 10-15% tail latency increase on the decode path. Noticed token-step slower across most models. PR #1423 landed this morning.

maria: Seen it in CI too — perf/regression-check job failed on the decode throughput benchmark.

ci-bot: perf job failure summary: bench/decode_throughput: baseline=980 TPS, current=860 TPS (-12.2%). See job: ci/perf/1423.

sam: Can you paste the pprof/top lines? Need to see where time is going.

alex: Pprof top (sampled wall):
```
      35.4%  fused_ops::decode_step
      22.1%  attention_kernels::compute
      18.5%  kv_cache::write_back (memcpy)
       9.2%  fallback_attn::dispatch
       7.8%  cuda_memcpy_async + sync
```
Seems like fused_ops and extra kv_cache copies dominate.

jin: I ran a quick git bisect across today's merges. Short summary:
```
git bisect start
# good: vbase (yesterday)
# bad: HEAD (after merges)
bisect run...
first bad commit identified: def4567 "fuse-attn-pass" -> introduces kernel selection changes
second suspect: abc1234 "kv-cache-write-fix" -> small increase (~5%)
```
def4567 is the likely culprit for the big jump.

maria: def4567 changed kernel selection heuristics to prefer fused_attn_v2 when seq_len>64, but the selector logic also inspects runtime batch shapes. Could be a corner where it picks fused_attn and then falls back mid-execution.

alex: Reproduced locally: for many short-seq workloads the selector miscomputes and we take a path that does an extra staging copy and then the fused kernel does an internal fallback, so we pay both costs.

rachel: KV cache logs show a new codepath writing out whole KV block each token:
```
kv_cache: wrote=6710886 bytes token=42 model=redwood-7b
kv_cache: previous_mode=append new_mode=full_write
```
That doubles memcpy work.

sam: There's also batching heuristic change in the same merge set? Some callers now batch across user requests differently, so batch_size reporting changed. That could move many requests into the wrong kernel regime.

alex: Quick mitigation options:
- revert def4567 (fastest)
- patch selector to add a conservative gating check: require seq_len*batch_size >= threshold AND no fallback flag set
- optimize kv_cache to avoid full_write when append is fine

maria: Revert would clear canary perf immediately. But we should follow with a test that ensures selector doesn't flip to degraded path for short seq workloads.

sam: I'm in favor of revert+small patch. Revert PR will include a microbenchmark and a new unit test for kernel selector.

ci-bot: perf/regression-check artifact: https://ci.redwood/archives/1423/perf.html

alex: Example patch snippet for gate:
```c++
if (batch_size * seq_len < FUSED_THRESHOLD || kernel_fallback_expected) {
  use_legacy_attn();
} else {
  use_fused_attn_v2();
}
```
We should also check has_partial_kv_flag before choosing fused path.

maria: Opening revert PR now: #1437 revert def4567 + add perf test. Will attach before/after benchmark.

alex: Blocking rollout for the release until we confirm revert. Canary pool held. @deploy-bot please pause any automated rollouts.

deploy-bot: Rollouts paused for channel=canary per request by alex. Action: hold until manual resume.

jin: Attached bisect log and repro script:
```
# bisect-log.txt
good: abc... yesterday
bad: def4567
tested commits: abc1234 -> +5%
def4567 -> +12%
repro: scripts/repro_decode_shortseq.sh --model redwood-7b --seq 32 --batch 4 --iters 200
```

rachel: I'll look into KV cache write mode — seems like the new path flips mode for edge batched shapes. Might be a zero-cost fix (one-line change).

sam: Action items:
- maria: open revert PR #1437 (in progress)
- alex + rachel: quick patch to avoid full_write in kv_cache and add unit test
- jin: add bisect summary to the PR and attach repro script
- sam: add perf microbench job to CI gating for decode path

maria: PR #1437 created. Benchmarks in PR show decode_throughput: before=980 TPS, after-revert=975 TPS, HEAD=860 TPS. Patch includes test coverage for kernel selection edge case.

alex: Great. Once revert merges, we'll re-run canary. If stable, proceed with a smaller, audited re-introduce of fused-attn changes with KV and selector fixes.

sam: Follow-up: add telemetry to runtime to record chosen kernel variant and fallback count per request (low-overhead counters). Will help detect regressions earlier.

maria: tagging owners: alex, rachel, jin, sam. Will follow up in PR thread. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks all. Keeping this thread updated with bench numbers.
